newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC FACE SEASON START WITHOUT CADETE, DI CANIO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC FACE SEASON START WITHOUT CADETE, DI CANIO.

text.p: Celtic face the prospect of starting the season without their two top stars.

Jorge Cadete and Paolo Di Canio -- who between them netted 48 goals last season -- have both failed to join their team-mates at the club's pre-season training camp in the Netherlands but for different reasons.
Portugese striker Cadete has been missing for a week in his native Lisbon, where it has been confirmed that he has been seeing a doctor over "family problems."
Meanwhile, former AC Milan winger Di Canio is working out on his own in Glasgow after refusing three times to travel to Arnhem where the squad are preparing under new head coach Wim Jansen.

Celtic must play a UEFA Cup qualifying round tie on July 23 and 30 -- the draw for which is made on Wednesday -- but the likelihood is that neither of their foreign stars will be fit to play, even if each resolves his problem.

Both have been involved in contract rows with Celtic chairman Fergus McCann but the latest double desertion has left the club's supporters concerned about the forthcoming league campaign, which starts on August 2.

Celtic had heard nothing from Cadete until Monday when they finally received a letter from his doctor, saying the 28-year-old player was unfit to travel to Glasgow where he should have started training week ago.
A Portugese psychiatrist, Dr Jose Tropa, has stated: "Mr Cadete is not in a very good psychological condition at the moment."
"This is not a medical condition but has been caused by family problems on his mind. I cannot reveal exactly what is wrong but I have told Celtic in my letter. He will play football again soon."

Cadete's wife Annabel left Glasgow some months ago, saying she could not settle there and the former Sporting Lisbon star has twice had request for a club transfer refused recently, while Spanish club Real Sociedad were told he was not for sale.
Di Canio's insistence that he knows best on how to recover from a virus -- for which Celtic gave him an extra week's holiday at home in Italy -- is certain to earn him another hefty fine.

The ex-Juventus and Napoli player, the idol of the Celtic support, was fined 25,000 pounds ($42,000) in May for criticising club chief McCann and the refusal to go to the Netherlands is expected to attract at least a similar punishment.
